claim: In centralized-data-service mapToClickHouseColumnType, the switch statement only matches PostgreSQL type names and falls back to String for unmapped strings like INT64, UINT8, FLOAT64, or DATETIME64.
evidence:
REF: /Users/trainguyen/Documents/work/data-hub/centralized-data-service/internal/service/master/master_ddl_generator_clickhouse.go:47-70
func mapToClickHouseColumnType(pgType string, isNullable bool) string {
	upper := strings.ToUpper(strings.TrimSpace(pgType))
	var baseType string
	switch {
	case upper == "BIGINT" || upper == "INT8":
		baseType = "Int64"
	case upper == "INTEGER" || upper == "INT" || upper == "INT4":
		baseType = "Int32"
	case upper == "SMALLINT" || upper == "INT2":
		baseType = "Int16"
	case upper == "BOOLEAN" || upper == "BOOL":
		baseType = "UInt8"
	case upper == "DOUBLE PRECISION" || upper == "FLOAT8" || upper == "REAL" || upper == "FLOAT4":
		baseType = "Float64"
	case strings.HasPrefix(upper, "NUMERIC") || strings.HasPrefix(upper, "DECIMAL"):
		baseType = "Decimal(38, 10)"
	case upper == "TIMESTAMPTZ" || upper == "TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE" || upper == "TIMESTAMP":
		baseType = "DateTime64(3, 'UTC')"
	case upper == "DATE":
		baseType = "Date32"
	default:
		baseType = "String"
	}
flow: generateClickHouseDDL and reconcileClickHouseColumn call mapToClickHouseColumnType(r.DataType, true).
